mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) reflects strong labor market conditions, which typically boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS is rising, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.4% signals an overheating labor market that may trigger Federal Reserve tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances (UNRATE < 3.4%), or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 108.0 and housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1300.0, it indicates synchronized strength in manufacturing and residential construction, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through improved economic growth expectations.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances (INDPRO>108.0 and HOUST>1300.0), or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), the Federal Reserve's policy rate hikes compress equity valuations through higher discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 1350.0 signals strong consumer demand for residential construction, which typically boosts economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances (HOUST > 1350.0), or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) rises above 258.0, it indicates accelerating inflation, which may prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances (CPIAUCSL > 258.0), or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The joint rise in the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 1.5% and inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 258.0 signals an active monetary tightening cycle, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances (FEDFUNDS>1.5 and CPIAUCSL>258.0), or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) reflects robust manufacturing output, which typically supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is rising, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
